FLASHCARD SET · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Weather, Seasons & What We Wear flashcards.

Twenty-nine cards about the sky over our heads and the clothes on our bodies: the sun and clouds, rain and rainbows, storms and snow, the four seasons, and the umbrella, raincoat, sun hat and winter coat that match each kind of day. Look out the window, pick the matching card, and the weather itself becomes the lesson.

These cards belong to Class 34 · Weather, Seasons & What We Wear on the Kiddo School learning path.

Every card in the set.

Every card is right here on one page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Read every card right here.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Open the day with the sky

    Stand at the window or step outside and ask "What is the sky doing today?" Then find the card that matches — sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, foggy or snowy. The real sky is the answer key, so every day the set gets a check-up.

  2. 02

    Dress the part

    After a weather card, open the matching clothing card: rain goes with the raincoat and boots, a hot sunny day goes with the sun hat and sunglasses. Let your child pick that piece of clothing for real — dressing themselves is the practice.

  3. 03

    Say the words, then spot them

    Every card page has a "Say it together" line in parent words. Say it on the doorstep, at the bus stop, in the bath — then celebrate loudly when your child spots a rainbow, a fog or a snowy branch out in the world first.

  4. 04

    Keep a week of weather

    Pin seven papers to the fridge, one per day, and let your child draw the day’s sky on each. On day seven, look back together: which sky came most often? That little chart is a child’s first forecast.

      Sun Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The sun is the bright star that lights our days and warms our skin — the reason we can see, play and grow things.

      Teaching tips

      What this card is for

      One bright thing to name on every walk — the sky's fixed point.

      A quick weather game

      Tape it to a spoon and let it rise over the sofa arm.

      What they take from it

      Light, warmth and why gardens grow — the sun as the day's engine.

      Print it like this

      Plain A4 is fine; cardstock lasts longer on a sunny windowsill.

      Tip of the day

      Yellow crayon day: every drawing today gets a sun corner.

      Teach it, step by step

      Print it like this
